anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet, the WS2812B status LED (D7) has its serial data input DIN (pin 1) wired straight to the +3V3 rail, the same net as its VDD (pin 4); DOUT (pin 2) is a no-connect and no MCU GPIO net reaches the device.
anomalies.expected: The WS2812B data input must be driven by a controllable MCU GPIO so the firmware can set the LED color per the running state. The specification lists only VDD on +3V3 for the status LED and describes it as a firmware-driven status indicator, so DIN tied to a supply rail is a deviation.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (page 1/4): D7 WS2812B — pin 1 DIN wired to '+3V3' arrow, pin 4 VDD to '+3V3', pin 2 DOUT marked with no-connect 'X'
Exposes status over Wi-Fi via a small webserver ... and a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1).

anomalies.impact: With DIN held permanently high, the WS2812B latches an all-ones (full-white) pattern and can never be updated, so the onboard status LED no longer reflects the controller state (running, fault, idle, etc.) as intended.

parsed.summary: The power, heater-switch, thermocouple-SPI and USB/fan interfaces match the specification (allowing for the build's renumbered references), but the WS2812B status LED's data input (D7 pin 1) is tied directly to +3V3 instead of a controllable GPIO, which would lock the status LED on and defeat its purpose.
